how_read: scripts/kb/fetch_wiki_live_pages.py --api https://gta.fandom.com/api.php --titles <pages> (page text as rendered by the wiki, link markup removed). Every quoted sentence below was checked, by script, to appear word for word in the page text read at the revision named. Several GTA Wiki pages cover many games; a line states a Grand Theft Auto III fact only where the page says so for GTA III or for the 3D games as a whole (GTA III included) with no exception for GTA III. The library's game entry and older notes are for the Definitive Edition, but every page read describes the original game (only the hidden packages page mentions the Definitive Edition, for an achievement); lines that state something that could differ between the two (prices, first-person aiming, pager notices, saving and health) begin "In the original game". Gang pages mix games in their infoboxes, so only text that names GTA III, or the Gangs in GTA III page, is used for gang facts.

lines.line: Summary: A small Latin American gang that holds the Hepburn Heights district of Portland and is not well armed.

quoted: The Diablos are a Latin American gang led by El Burro and based in Hepburn Heights, Portland.
They are a fairly small gang, and not very well armed.
Hepburn Heights is now completely under Diablos' control.

lines.line: Weak points: They are lightly armed: baseball bats only, except in missions, where they also carry guns.

quoted: they are poorly armed and use only baseball bats (guns in missions only).

lines.line: Looks like: Two outfits: red bandana, dark blue jacket and light blue jeans; or blue bandana, olive cargo pants and the same jacket.

quoted: There are two variants of Diablos - one with a red bandana, light blue jeans, and a dark blue jacket, and another one with a blue bandana, a dark blue jacket, and olive cargo pants.

lines.line: Tips: Diablo Stallions are their cars in every game they appear in. The Uptown Yardies are their arch rivals.

quoted: They drive Diablo Stallions in all of the games they are featured in.
They are arch rivals of the Uptown Yardies.

lines.line: Summary: A Chinese criminal gang that holds Chinatown plus the Callahan Point area of Portland.

quoted: The Triads are a Chinese criminal organization that arrived in the city in 1997, with help from the Sicilian Mafia. They control the Chinatown and the Callahan Point areas of Portland

lines.line: Looks like: Members dress in blue boiler suits with black bandannas.

quoted: Triad members wear blue boiler suits and black bandannas.

lines.line: Tips: Expect baseball bats or pistols from members. The Leone Family are their enemies, and the rivalry is fierce.

quoted: They carry baseball bats or pistols.
and are the enemies of the Leone Family.
They have a fierce rivalry with the Triads.

lines.line: Summary: An Italian mafia family based mainly in Saint Mark's, Portland, with a stake in Trenton, Chinatown and the Red Light District; the wiki names it the most dangerous gang, thanks to its shotguns.

quoted: the Leone Crime Family is an Italian mafia
They are based in Portland, in particular Saint Mark's, but also have interests in the Red Light District, Chinatown and Trenton.
The most dangerous gang is the Leone Family, since they have powerful shotguns

lines.line: Looks like: Their men dress in black suits and some add sunglasses; the gang car is the Mafia Sentinel, which is gray in the original game.

quoted: In Grand Theft Auto III and Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories, Leone henchmen wear black suits, some with sunglasses.
The official gang car of the Leone family is the Mafia Sentinel, a modified jet black (gray in GTA III) version of the Sentinel

lines.line: Tips: Their shotguns can blow up an ordinary car in two shots, so a vehicle within their range does not last long. They are fierce rivals of the Triads.

quoted: since they have powerful shotguns, which can easily blow up a normal car in two shots.
capable of making quick work of vehicles if the player drives within range of their shotguns.
They have a fierce rivalry with the Triads.

lines.line: Summary: A drug cartel from Colombia that seized control of some of Shoreside Vale and Staunton Island and is deeply tied to the drug trade.

quoted: The Colombian Cartel or simply the Cartel is a Colombian drug cartel
they quickly gained control of parts of Staunton Island and Shoreside Vale. They are heavily involved in the drugs trade

lines.line: Looks like: Members dress in Hawaiian shirts and combat pants, with cowboy boots and Akruba-style hats, in the original game.

quoted: Cartel members wear Hawaiian shirts, combat pants, Akruba-style hats and cowboy boots in GTA III.

lines.line: Tips: The Yakuza and the Leone Family are its biggest enemies. In the original game the gang drives the Cartel Cruiser.

quoted: Cartel Cruiser (GTA III & GTA Liberty City Stories)
Their main enemies are the Leone Family and the Yakuza.

lines.line: Summary: A mostly Jamaican gang from Staunton Island; these days you only find them in Newport, though they also seem to deal near Liberty Campus.

quoted: The Uptown Yardies or simply the Yardies are an African-Caribbean (mostly Jamaican) criminal organization led by King Courtney, based in Staunton Island.
The Yardies can now be solely found in Newport, but appear to be dealing around the Liberty Campus as well

lines.line: Looks like: Members wear a short-sleeved black hoodie with a tan vest, tan pants and brown shoes, and the gang's two member models look alike.

quoted: In GTA III, Uptown Yardie members wear a black short-sleeved hoodie, tan vest and pants, and brown shoes. Both skins of the Yardies appear visually identical in this game.

lines.line: Tips: Members carry baseball bats; the wiki also lists a pistol and, in some missions, an Uzi. Their Yardie Lobo lowriders are the only cars here with hydraulic suspension, and the Diablos are their rivals.

quoted: Carried by members of the Diablos, Triads and the Uptown Yardies.
- Pistol - Baseball Bat - Uzi (Uzi Rider & The Whole 9 Yardies)
The gang drives Yardie Lobo lowriders, which are unique for their use of hydraulic suspension in GTA III.
Their rivals are the Diablos

lines.line: Summary: The Army starts chasing you when your wanted level hits six stars, a step after the FBI at five stars, and the Rhino tank appears at that level too.

quoted: After the player gains a six-star wanted level in any game set in the 3D Universe, the Army will begin to chase the player.
The FBI will only appear when the player's wanted level reaches five stars, before the army arrives at six stars.
the Rhino appears when the player attains a six-star wanted level.

lines.line: Weak points: A Rhino is nearly immune to small-arms fire. Explosives and flame weapons (molotovs, the flamethrower) hurt it, and when you fight a military one the windshield is the only soft spot.

quoted: The Rhino is practically invincible to small arms fire and collisions; only explosives and the gun mounted on the Police Maverick can inflict damage. Additionally, flame weapons such as the molotov cocktails and the flamethrower are able to damage the tank.
Only the windshield can be considered a weak spot, although this is only evident when confronting military-controlled Rhinos to hijack them.

lines.line: Tips: In the original game, soldiers drop grenades when you kill them. The authorities seldom fire the cannon of the Rhino.

quoted: Dropped by Military soldiers when killed.
Law enforcement tends not to use the main cannon of the vehicle.

lines.line: Summary: Armor is a second layer of protection on top of your health, taking hits from gunfire, blasts and flames. In the original game it shows up as a shield icon and gives nearly as many hit points as full health.

quoted: The body armor's primary function is to serve as padding for the player health, in effect extending the player's resilience to damage from gunfire, explosions and fire.
When included in GTA III, the pickup assumed the appearance of a shield icon
In all of its appearances, armor now offers nearly the same amount of hit points as the player's full health, doubling the player's resistance to damage.

lines.line: Uses: In Grand Theft Auto III, it also soaks up damage from falls, vehicle hits while you are on foot, and melee blows too.

quoted: In addition, armor can now pad injuries from falls, collisions with vehicles on foot, and even melee attacks

lines.line: Tips: In the original game, it costs $3,000 at Ammu-Nation after you finish Last Requests, and getting into a Police or SWAT Enforcer truck also gives you some. Collecting 50 hidden packages puts a permanent armor pickup outside every safehouse.

quoted: $3,000 (GTA III & GTA Advance)
Last Requests (GTA III)
Ammu-Nation (3D Universe, GTA Chinatown Wars, GTA V, GTA Online)
drawn_from.note: The first three quotes are cells of the page's infobox table (Price, Unlocked After, Available from), joined into one sentence.

quoted: as well as entering the Police/SWAT Enforcer trucks.
For each 10 Hidden Packages collected, a permanent spawn point for a specific item is created in front of all safehouses.
50 Packages: Body Armor

lines.line: Summary: A pickup that fills your health to the maximum; in Grand Theft Auto III they are found in front of every hospital and spread around Liberty City, often in places like shopping centers, parks and rest stops.

quoted: Health pickups scattered around the map can restore the player's health to the maximum level.
In Grand Theft Auto III, health pickups can be found in front of all hospitals and scattered throughout Liberty City, often in recreational areas such as rest stops, parks, and shopping centers.

lines.line: Uses: Health is shown as a number that starts out capped at 100%, and paying a prostitute can push it as high as 125%.

quoted: In Grand Theft Auto III and Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, the hit point system is replaced by a numbered counter, with its default maximum as 100%
Employing the services of a prostitute also replenishes health to a possible total of 125%.

lines.line: Tips: When your health hits zero you are wasted: you end up at the nearest hospital, pay a fee, lose every weapon and fail any mission you were on. In the original game, saving at a save point does not restore health, unlike in most other 3D games.

quoted: When the player's health is completely depleted, the protagonist is considered "wasted", and is then transported to the nearest hospital, after which a fee for healthcare will be assessed, and all weapons will be confiscated in the 2D and 3D Universes. Any mission that may have been in progress at the time is considered as failed.
by visiting a save point to save the game (in all 3D Universe titles, save for GTA III and Grand Theft Auto Advance

lines.line: Summary: Pills lying around Liberty City that give a short burst of speed while time seems to slow down.

quoted: Adrenaline pills are items scattered around Liberty City in Grand Theft Auto III
When collected by the player, the adrenaline pills give the player a temporary boost of speed while seemingly slowing down time.

lines.line: Uses: Your aim keeps its normal speed while everything else slows, which is handy against police and gangs, and you also jump further than usual.

quoted: While the game's speed is slowed down, the player's aiming speed is the same as it would normally be, which is handy when engaged in gun battles with the police, gangs or during rampages. The player can also jump further than normal.

lines.line: Tips: Getting into a vehicle ends the speed boost. One lies in Trenton behind the big sign on the roof of Liberty Pharmaceuticals.

quoted: Strangely, entering a vehicle resets the speed to normal again.
Trenton – Behind the large sign on top of Liberty Pharmaceuticals.

lines.line: Summary: In Grand Theft Auto III each police bribe is a spinning police badge shaped like a star; picking it up drops your wanted level one star. The wiki calls it a free alternative to getting your car resprayed.

quoted: the bribe appears as a rotating, star-shaped police badge pickup that will reduce the player's wanted level by one star when picked up
the pickup is intended as an cost-free alternative to respraying the player's vehicle at a spray shop

lines.line: Uses: In Grand Theft Auto III, a bribe does not stop the stronger forces already after you, such as the Army, SWAT or the FBI, though no more of their vehicles turn up. A Police Maverick is the one exception: at three stars it breaks off, and you drop to two.

quoted: any higher-level police presence (Military, SWAT or FBI for example) in the area prior to obtaining the bribe will continue to pursue the player (assuming a wanted level is still in place), but no more law enforcement vehicles appear. The one exception is the Police Maverick, which will disengage from pursuit of a player with a three-star wanted level upon obtaining a police bribe (reducing their wanted level to two stars).

lines.line: Tips: Bribes are rare, so learn where they are: a few are in plain sight and others are tucked out of view. In Grand Theft Auto III, some can only be reached by jumping a vehicle.

quoted: its scarcity makes the tactic more difficult unless the player memorizes their locations. Police bribe locations vary widely, with some showing up in obvious locations, while others are well hidden from plain view.
In the 3D Universe, some bribe stars are placed in positions that require the player to execute a jump with a vehicle in order to obtain them.

lines.line: Summary: Liberty City hides 100 packages, each a white bale tied up with brown adhesive tape that pays $1,000; every tenth one unlocks a lasting item pickup outside the safehouses.

quoted: There are 100 Hidden Packages located all around Liberty City
They take the appearance of a white bale sealed with brown adhesive tape.
Each Hidden Package will award the player with $1,000.

lines.line: Uses: In the original game a pager message announces each reward, and a pickup for that item then waits permanently outside every safehouse: 10 pistol, 20 Uzi, 30 grenades, 40 shotgun, 50 body armor, 60 molotov cocktails, 70 AK47, 80 sniper rifle, 90 M16, and at 100 the rocket launcher plus $1,000,000.

quoted: For each 10 Hidden Packages collected, a permanent spawn point for a specific item is created in front of all safehouses. The player will be notified of each reward via pager.
10 Packages: Pistol
20 Packages: Uzi
30 Packages: Grenades
40 Packages: Shotgun
50 Packages: Body Armor
60 Packages: Molotov Cocktails
70 Packages: AK47
80 Packages: Sniper Rifle
90 Packages: M16
100 Packages: Rocket Launcher and $1,000,000

lines.line: Tips: Pick them up on foot; driving over one does not count. You need all of them for 100% completion.

quoted: which the player must find and collect while on foot. These items cannot be collected while on a vehicle.
Collecting all Hidden Packages is a requirement for the 100% completion.

lines.line: Summary: A one-shot rocket launcher that can wreck almost any vehicle or pedestrian; in the original game you can buy it for $25,000 at Phil Cassidy's Army Surplus in Rockford, Staunton Island, once you have finished Arms Shortage.

quoted: Single-shot
It is capable of massive destruction and power, with the ability to destroy nearly all vehicles and pedestrians.
Rockford, Staunton Island – Available to buy from Phil Cassidy's Army Surplus after completion of Arms Shortage. ($25,000)

lines.line: Uses: Its weight holds you to a jog and rules out jumping while it is in your hands. Rockets go exactly where you aim, and it can bring down police helicopters that chase you, but it will not finish off a tank such as the Rhino in one hit.

quoted: Its heavy weight will cause the protagonist to be slowed to a jogging pace and not be able to jump while the weapon is equipped except from Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories and onwards. The rocket is also very accurate, as it always travels right where the aiming sight is placed. Much like in the 2D Universe, the Rocket Launcher cannot destroy tanks like the Rhino instantly.
is also able to take out pursuing police helicopters during wanted levels.

lines.line: Tips: Gather every one of the 100 hidden packages and one appears at every safehouse. Another is in Cedar Grove, at the western end of The Homes (the stretch nearest Cochrane Dam): the big pink house there has one on its roof, along the western side.

quoted: Spawns at every safehouse after collecting all 100 hidden packages.
Cedar Grove, Shoreside Vale – On the west side of the roof of the large pink house at the west end of The Homes (closest to Cochrane Dam).

lines.line: Summary: In the original game the AK47 trades damage for speed: it fires very fast but hits weakly. Ammu-Nation in Newport sells it for $3,000 after you finish Last Requests.

quoted: In Grand Theft Auto III, the AK47 behaves rather differently from later games, as it is depicted with a very high rate of fire but low damage
Newport, Staunton Island - Available to buy from Ammu-Nation after completion of Last Requests ($3,000).

lines.line: Uses: In the original game you cannot aim it in first person, unlike the M16. Its recoil is gentler, but the M16 beats it otherwise: it does far more damage, fires faster and holds twice as many rounds.

quoted: Unlike the M16 (and unlike the Ruger from Grand Theft Auto: Vice City), it cannot be aimed in first person. It has lower recoil than the M16, but other than that it is outclassed by it, as the M16 deals way more damage and has a much higher fire rate than it, as well as having double the AK's magazine capacity.

lines.line: Tips: Collecting 70 hidden packages puts one at each safehouse. There is also one in Trenton, behind the big sign on the roof of Liberty Pharmaceuticals, beside adrenaline, health and armor pickups; reach it by jumping from the elevated tracks.

quoted: Safehouses – Spawn at each safehouse after collecting 70 Hidden Packages.

Trenton, Portland - On top of Liberty Pharmaceuticals (behind the large sign) near an adrenaline icon, a health icon, and a body armor icon. Jump from the elevated tracks near the northeast side of the large complex to access.

lines.line: Summary: A thrown bottle that can light up vehicles and any cluster of pedestrians; using one usually brings a wanted level of up to three stars.

quoted: The Molotov Cocktail can set vehicles and groups of pedestrians on fire.
Use of the Molotov will normally result in a wanted level amounting up to three stars.

lines.line: Uses: Anyone on foot who stands close to the flames burns to death. Molotovs are one of the flame weapons that can hurt a Rhino.

quoted: Victims on foot will catch fire and die if close enough to the flames.
flame weapons such as the molotov cocktails and the flamethrower are able to damage the tank.

lines.line: Tips: In the other 3D games a molotov or two will down a police helicopter, but not in Grand Theft Auto III. In Grand Theft Auto III, collecting 60 hidden packages puts one at every safehouse, and the pickup on the upper level of Liberty Campus's courtyard gives 10.

quoted: one or two Molotovs is capable of taking down an airborne NPC helicopter, making it suitable to fend off pursuing Police Mavericks above during a three-star wanted level on foot (except for Grand Theft Auto III).
Spawns at every safehouse after collecting 60 Hidden Packages.
Liberty Campus, Staunton Island – On the upper level on the north part of the Campus Courtyard next to the east set of stairs. This pickup will give you 10 molotovs.

lines.line: Summary: A heavy armored tank with a cannon that turns up once your wanted level reaches six stars; it runs on wheels rather than tracks.

quoted: the Rhino appears when the player attains a six-star wanted level.
Contrary to most real-life tanks, the Rhino uses individual wheels instead of continuous tracks

lines.line: Uses: Small arms fire and crashes do almost nothing to it, and any vehicle it hits blows up or catches fire, which is handy against wanted levels because police cars tend to ram you. Its cannon is devastating to most vehicles.

quoted: The Rhino is practically invincible to small arms fire and collisions

any vehicle hit will either explode instantly or end up burning instead. This makes the vehicle ideal for dealing with wanted levels, as most police vehicles have a tendency to hit the player's vehicle in an attempt to block their path.
The Rhino is equipped with a cannon turret, which has devastating firepower against most vehicles.

lines.line: Looks like: Boxy and truck-like, with three axles, a slim windshield, big doors along both sides and a turret on its roof; it only comes in a faded green.

quoted: The Rhino is depicted as a block-shaped vehicle with a truck-style, three-axle chassis, a narrow windshield and large doors on each side, along with the corresponding turret on top.
The Rhino only spawns in a worn green color

lines.line: Tips: It handles poorly: even at low speed it turns in a wide circle, and it accelerates very slowly. Its side doors also leave you open to being busted or dragged out by a hostile pedestrian. You can get one at Portland Harbor after you have collected every emergency vehicle for Import/Export.

quoted: its handling is pretty inferior compared to other heavy vehicles, as, even at low speeds, it has a wide turning radius.
it has very low acceleration
The slow speed and presence of doors on the sides makes the player easily vulnerable to being busted by law enforcers or being otherwise pulled out by any hostile pedestrian
It can be obtained at Portland Harbor once all emergency vehicles have been collected for Import/Export.
